meta.description: Located on the third floor of the Ryan Center, this work center is dedicated to delivering vital operational augmentation to active duty Air Operations Centers worldwide, ensuring air component commanders in any theater receive critical expertise, tactical integration, and sustained operational continuity. Operating within a standard professional office environment, personnel routinely carry out typical administrative, planning, and coordination duties, including drafting operational correspondence, managing communications, conducting reachback support, and maintaining operational readiness records.

meta.medicalFacility:
During normal duty hours on weekdays, personnel are to report to Langley AFB Hospital for assessment and treatment of injuries suffered while on-the-job. Civilian employees may elect to receive treatment from their personal physician.

If the injury or medical condition does not permit the injured person to first report to Langley AFB Hospital the individuals should be treated at the closest medical facility.

The Base Clinic is located at 77 Nealy Avenue. Also, advise member that the Base Clinic does provides 24 hour emergency service. Call (757) 225-7630, or DSN 575-7630.
meta.evacuationRoute: Primary route is the North Stairwell. Secondary route is the South Stairwell. Assembly location for the 710 COS is the Southeast corner of the Ryan Center parking lot.
meta.shelterInPlace: There are six SIP locations located within the Ryan Center. All personnel on the 1st floor collateral area report to conference room A121. All personnel on the 1st floor SCIF areas report to D105. All personnel on the 2d floor collateral areas report to conference rooms B201 and/or D209. All 3rd floor personnel report to conference room F303 and/or the Ops floor across the hall.
meta.activeShooterMethods:
An active shooter is an individual actively engaged in killing or attempting to kill people. In most cases, active shooters use firearms and there is no pattern or method to their selection of victims. In some cases, active shooters use improvised explosive devices to create additional victims and to impede first responders.

All personnel should know the following term:
LOCKDOWN – An announcement used on Air Force installations as a security measure to confine and restrict movement. All individuals, including military uniformed services, federal employees, contractors, dependents, and other people on an installation as a guest are required to restrict their movement when lockdown is declared. During lockdown, no person may enter or exit another area until the all clear is broadcasted; unless movement is required to escape from a dangerous place or situation.

When a LOCKDOWN/ACTIVE SHOOTER is announced:
The Senior Person on Duty (SPOD) for each facility will ensure a person immediately proceeds to the building entrance to implement the following measures:
a. If it is safe to do so, retrieve “Lockdown in Progress” sign (kept behind the hard-copy EAP next to the security binder) and post over badging keypad or on door.
b. Lock the CDX-9/10. Referring to the image below, pull out the Life Safety pin and turn the Pedestrian Door Lock knob clockwise until it stops to secure the door and to impede/delay a possible cleared active shooter from badging/entering into the facility.
Evacuate – If an escape route is accessible, evacuate the immediate area! Leave your belongings behind and help others evacuate, if possible, but evacuate even if others will not agree to follow you. Call 911 or 764-5091/5092 when you are safe. Once evacuated, prevent others from entering the area. Follow any law enforcement instructions and, if in view of approaching law enforcement personnel, keep your hands visible. Do not attempt to move wounded individuals.

Barricade – If evacuation is not possible, find a place to create a barricade between you and the active shooter. Your barricade location should be where you are less likely to be found by the active shooter, provide you protection, and not restrict your options for movement. If possible, lock the door and or block the door with heavy furniture. Turn off any lights and cover first floor windows. Remain quiet and silence any devices that may give away your hiding place. If safe to do so, call 911 or 764-5091/5092 to alert law enforcement of your location and stay on the phone.

Fight – As a last resort, and only when your life is in imminent danger, attempt to disrupt and/or incapacitate the shooter. Personnel should use whatever means possible to overpower the subject to save further lives. Use the minimum force necessary to subdue the shooter; however, deadly force is authorized when an individual reasonably believes they or others in the area are in immediate danger of death or serious bodily harm.

Information to provide to law enforcement/security forces when you are able/safe to do so:
Number of active shooters, if more than one
Location of the shooter (s)
Physical description of the shooter (s)
Time you observed the shooter (s)
Number and type of weapons held by the shooter (s)
Number of potential victims at the location

When law enforcement/security forces arrive, their primary purpose is to stop the shooter as soon as possible. Responders will proceed directly to the area in which the last shots were heard/reported and will not stop to help injured persons until the shooter is confirmed to be neutralized. Your responsibilities are to:
Remain calm and follow instructions
Place any items in your hands on the ground and raise immediately raise your hands and spread your fingers. Keep hands visible at all times!
Do not impede law enforcement officers’ movements, such as holding on to them for safety or asking them for help or directions when evacuating
Provide any information that may assist them in countering the threat
Avoid pointing, screaming and/or yelling
Move quickly to the assembly point and stay there until the situation is under control; do not leave until instructed to do so by law enforcement.

After the active shooter situation is neutralized; stay away from the incident area. Listen to local radio, television stations, and/or the installation’s warning and notification system for the latest information. Notify your friends and family of your condition; however, use phone services sparingly so they remain open for emergency responders. Finally, know and recognize the signs of incident related stress and seek assistance as needed.
meta.safetyBoardLocation: Found at the E307 Corridor by the water fountain and Men's Restroom.
meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
Requirements of Air Force Traffic Safety Program, including mandatory use of seat belts and helmets, speed limits, local traffic hazards, personal risk management and cell phone prohibition while operating a GMV or PMV on base. If Applicable, Discuss Motorcycle Safety Training Requirements Before Riding A Motorcycle. (AFI 91-202 para. A4.1.9)

Cell phone use while driving is prohibited. If you are driving and you need to take a call, use hands free device or safely pull off to the side of the road, put your hazards lights on and take the call.

All newly assigned and PCS personnel who are motorcycle riders will be required to process through the commander or designated representative. Unit commander or designated MSR(s) will provide an initial briefing to all new or newly assigned motorcycle riders within 30 days from initial assignment, identification as a rider or purchase of a motorcycle.
